## 2. What it leans on

- **morale_diff** 0.811 (was 0.653): own minus enemy morale summed over players (boosts +, death penalty -)
- **knights_diff** 0.414 (was 0.486): own minus enemy pit knights alive

Proposed 2026-11-06 from OG comms ([ohno v NwAy]: 'this way we don't lose footmen'); moved in as footmen alive after chunk 4, then counted as losses after chunk 5 (Denning): a footman only enters the replay once something touches it, so 'alive' marked a base that was visited and read backwards (-42 points at +4); deaths are always recorded
- **alive_diff** 0.227 (was 0.164): own minus enemy players alive
- **stand** 0.22 (was 0.211): who holds the flag stand: 1 own, 0 nobody, -1 enemy

- **flag_lead** 0.174 (was 0.154): seconds up (+) or down (-) on flags: enemy's response minus own on the next capture exchange
- **lord_dps_own** 0.172 (was 0.168): own build's measured Lord damage per second if all its non-healers were at the Lord
- **lord_dps_enemy** 0.171 (was 0.168): enemy build's measured Lord damage per second

- **knights_diff & map_bases_apart** 0.132 (new): own minus enemy pit knights alive TOGETHER WITH the map's distance between the two bases
- **archers_diff** 0.121 (was 0.107): own minus enemy pit archers alive

## 7. The usual play

Each choice against the most common one in that kind of decision, in win-chance points over the decision's window, adjusted for the situation, with a 90% range from resampling whole matches. CLEAR = the range excludes 0. Win chance comes from a model that never saw the match. The same comparison over the 30 s BEFORE the decision is a placebo test: a choice can't cause what came before it, so a clear difference there means the effect is partly who makes that choice.

## Does the advice work? (the goal test)

For each decision kind, the advice is built from five groups of matches and read on the sixth (unseen): teams whose choice matched the advice against teams whose didn't, win-chance change over the decision's window adjusted for the situation, 90% range from resampling whole matches. The advice = the best choice among the 15 most similar decisions (at least 5 cases, 2+ points better than the usual play), else the usual play. "Specific" = the advice differed from the usual play.

**3 of 13 kinds pass** (effect positive, range excludes 0): after_wipe, runner_choice, split_or_stay.

- after_wipe (821 decisions, 337 matches): matched the advice 75% of the time; effect of matching +1.6 points (90% +0.1 to +2.9; clear); raw 0.3 matched against -2.0 not; specific advice in 6% of cases, raw effect there +2.4. Most recommended: pushed the pit (740), took the flag (63), reset (18).
- boost_clock (1322 decisions, 330 matches): matched the advice 22% of the time; effect of matching +0.7 points (90% -0.2 to +1.6; not clear); raw 0.3 matched against -0.4 not; specific advice in 1% of cases. Most recommended: not running, fought (478), running, advanced (267), not running, fell back (184), running, fought (149), not running, advanced (108), not running, held (57).
- eight_v_eight_or_flag (3264 decisions, 328 matches): matched the advice 74% of the time; effect of matching -0.4 points (90% -1.7 to +0.8; not clear); raw -0.4 matched against -0.4 not; specific advice in 11% of cases, raw effect there +2.0. Most recommended: flag game (2783), commit all 8 (481).
- enemy_pickup (4443 decisions, 339 matches): matched the advice 20% of the time; effect of matching -0.4 points (90% -1.3 to +0.5; not clear); raw -0.3 matched against 0.0 not; specific advice in 1% of cases, raw effect there +2.3. Win points for the team it happened to, from 356 matches. **Result** = how matches actually ended against what a win model that never saw the match expected just before (so it includes what the event usually led to); **model** = the win model's own change over the next 30 s. Both against matched moments without the event (same minute and win chance). A gap between the two points at a win-model curve to check.

## The TQs

Denning's four questions, each from the batch's matches. The why comes from forensics and events (every number placed against the same role or situation in every stored match); the different play comes only from measurement: the usual play's choice effects (usual.py), node models read again with the variable changed (models that never saw the match, changes priced in win points with values.py), options that were ready and unused, and benchmarks. Points = win-chance points.
